🔔 Kalshi ruling puts CFTC prediction rules at risk 

⚠️ A federal appeals court ruled on Aug. 28 that Kalshi had not shown Nevada’s regulation of its sports-event contracts was likely preempted by federal commodities law. The unanimous decision allows Nevada gaming authorities to enforce state requirements while litigation continues.

⚠️ Kalshi argued that its sports-event contracts qualified as swaps under the Commodity Exchange Act. Because Kalshi operates a CFTC-regulated designated contract market, it said federal jurisdiction displaced Nevada’s gaming laws. The Ninth Circuit rejected that argument at the preliminary-injunction stage. It found that the contracts likely fell outside the applicable meaning of “swap” because they functioned as sports bets. The panel consequently rejected Kalshi’s express, conflict and field-preemption arguments.

📣 Circuit Judge Ryan Nelson wrote that “the CFTC is not a national gambling regulator.” The court said Kalshi’s broader interpretation lacked a limiting principle and did not fit the surrounding statutory framework. That prediction extends beyond the court’s direct holding. The opinion said Kalshi’s broad interpretation of “swap” “would raise concerns under the major-questions doctrine.” It did not hold that the doctrine categorically prevents the CFTC from regulating prediction markets.

💬 Hamas warns Israeli regime over escalating aggressions in occupied Al-Quds

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The Palestinian Islamic Resistance Movement (Hamas) warns of the consequences of the Israeli regime’s decision to launch a wide-scale military operation in the northeast of occupied Al-Quds, saying the move was part of the regime’s ongoing aggression against Palestinians.

In a statement, Hamas warned about what it described as the Israeli regime cabinet and military’s growing war crimes and the repercussions of a planned extensive military operation in Shuafat refugee camp and the town of Anata in northeastern occupied Al-Quds.
​
Meanwhile, Hamas also pointed to other aggressions by the Israeli regime, including a complete blockade, the closure of entrances, the destruction of infrastructure and widespread arrests of Palestinian citizens, saying, “The city of Al-Quds, its settlements and camps will remain solely Palestinian, and the attempts of the occupying regime to isolate, Judaize and impose control over it will fail in the face of the resistance and steadfastness of Al-Quds’s residents, their determination and stability in their land.”
​
Hamas added that the Israeli regime’s war machine would never be able to implement its settlement expansion plans.
​
“The occupation regime’s war machine will never be able to implement its settlement plans; our people will remain steadfast and committed to their land and rights until the end of the aggression and occupation,” the movement said.
​
